Championship standard Tom 4 known titles, including the 2016–18 three-peat and the 2024 205.30 championship eruption. Regular-season apex Mitch 55–33 Sleeper regular season, 13–1 in 2025, 1,894.88 PF, active 18-game win streak. Four known championships is not close to anyone else’s count. The three-peat created the league’s first dynasty, and the 2024 title proved it was not only an ancient-history accomplishment. Why Mitch has the dominance argument No current manager has a stronger reconstructed Sleeper regular-season profile. Schermerhorn is the surviving Shitter Bowl name for 2016. 2017 · champion: Tom Back-to-back Tom makes it two straight. Open season exhibit Champion Tom Season thesis Tom makes it two straight. What happened The first dynasty was already becoming obvious. Tom followed the inaugural surviving title with another championship. Permanent receipts Tom’s surviving high-score entry: 148.0 in Week 9 vs. Birch. Birch is the surviving Shitter Bowl name for 2017. 2018 · champion: Tom The three-peat Tom completes the league’s first dynasty. Open season exhibit Champion Tom Season thesis Tom completes the league’s first dynasty. What happened Three titles in three surviving seasons established the championship standard that still defines the league. Permanent receipts Tony’s 159.6 in Week 2 is the highest known pre-Sleeper score entry. Kuhl posted 150.5 in Week 9. Stilly is the surviving Shitter Bowl name for 2018. 2019 · champion: Birch The dynasty ends Birch finally breaks Tom’s run. Open season exhibit Champion Birch Season thesis Birch finally breaks Tom’s run. What happened Birch became the first manager in the surviving archive to knock Tom off the championship throne. Permanent receipts Birch’s title remains his first known championship. Evans is the surviving Shitter Bowl name for 2019. 2020 · champion: Koble The Sleeper origin story The best regular-season profile did not win. Koble did. Open season exhibit Champion Koble Season thesis The best regular-season profile did not win. Koble did. What happened Mitch had the best regular-season scoring profile, but Koble entered the playoffs at 6–7 and became the first Sleeper-era champion. Stilly finished 4–9 and became the first Sleeper-era SHITTER BOWL CHAMP. Permanent receipts Koble beat Kuhl, then Birch, then Mitch for the title. Stilly added Travis Kelce and later Lamar Jackson/J.K. Dobbins yet still finished last — an early proof that transactions and wins are different skills. Stew’s $22 Nyheim Hines claim is one of the earliest verified FAAB receipts. 2021 · champion: Tony Tony wins the trade market and the league A title built through elite consolidation. Open season exhibit Champion Tony Season thesis A title built through elite consolidation. What happened Tony won the championship while assembling one of the strongest transaction résumés in the archive. Permanent receipts Tony’s 2021 title roster was strengthened by major consolidation, including the verified Joe Mixon trade. An older archive summary mistakenly attached CMC to Tony’s transaction history; the raw Sleeper ledger disproves that attribution. Tony acquired Joe Mixon for James Robinson + Zack Moss — the cleanest pure-value win of the season. Birch went 11–2 after acquiring Lamar Jackson + Mark Andrews + Josh Jacobs. Kuhl’s transaction process was better than his 4–9 record suggested. 2022 · champion: Stover The best team did not win Stew dominated the regular season; Stover took the trophy. Open season exhibit Champion Stover Season thesis Stew dominated the regular season; Stover took the trophy. What happened Stew went 11–3, led the league in points and potential points, then lost the championship 99.22–48.16 to Stover. Permanent receipts Stew acquired Justin Jefferson and later Ja’Marr Chase in major trade wins. Tom’s CeeDee + DK + DeVonta consolidation was one of the year’s strongest aggregate-value trades. Tony spent $94 FAAB on Kenneth Walker — absurdly expensive and absolutely correct. Tony produced both the year’s known high (177.14) and low (60.66). 2023 · champion: Stilly Trade chaos, bench carnage, Stilly title Stew won the transaction count. EvansBrandon won the scoring title.
